definitions.explanation: informing someone about something before it happens
a short promotional video showing upcoming content

examples.japanese: {予告|よこく}なしに{訪問|ほうもん}された。
{一週間前|いっしゅうかんまえ}に{予告|よこく}してください。
examples.english: Please give us a week's notice.

examples.japanese: {犯人|はんにん}は{犯行|はんこう}を{予告|よこく}していた。
examples.english: The criminal had announced the crime in advance.

examples.japanese: {映画|えいが}の{予告|よこく}{編|へん}を{見|み}た。
{次回|じかい}{予告|よこく}が{楽|たの}しみだ。
examples.english: I look forward to the preview of the next episode.

examples.japanese: {予告|よこく}だけで{内容|ないよう}がわかってしまった。
examples.english: I could tell the whole story just from the trailer.

notes:
FORMATION:
{予|よ} (beforehand) + {告|こく} (announce) → announce beforehand

VERB FORM:
{予告|よこく}する (to give advance notice, to announce)

RELATED COMPOUNDS:
- {予告|よこく}{編|へん} (trailer, preview)
- {次回|じかい}{予告|よこく} (preview of next episode)
- {予告|よこく}{犯|はん} (crime announced in advance)
- {予告|よこく}なし (without notice)

RELATED WORDS:
- {告知|こくち} (notification, announcement)
- {通知|つうち} (notification)
- {事前|じぜん}{連絡|れんらく} (advance contact)
- トレーラー (trailer - loanword)

USAGE:
{予告|よこく}なし or {予告|よこく}なしに (without notice/warning) is a common phrase used when something happens unexpectedly or without prior communication.
